chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (the First) (peace be upon him).

He said: Nine things cause forgetfulness: eating apples (meaning sour ones), coriander and cheese; eating the remainder of a mouse; urinating in stagnant water; reading the writings on tombs; walking between two women; removing lice; and cupping at the pit of the head.

key_terms.السُّؤْرُ: The remainder of a drink or food left by someone or something
key_terms.النَّقْرَةُ: The pit of the head (between the eyes)

ai.seo_question: What are the nine things that cause forgetfulness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq attributes this list of nine causes for forgetfulness to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him), blending dietary advice with spiritual and physical practices. This narration reflects the Shia tradition of linking bodily health and environmental factors to cognitive and spiritual clarity, emphasizing that neglecting these areas can hinder one's ability to retain religious knowledge and divine guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-22 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dihqan, on the authority of Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdul-Hamid, on the authority of Abil Hassan - the first (i.e. Al-Kadhim) (MGB), “

Nine things cause forgetfulness: eating sour apples; eating coriander and cheese; eating remainders of mice; urinating in stagnant water; reading the writings on the tombs; going in between two women; killing lice; and cupping at the pit of the head.”
